{{Quote|The intensity will dissipate to the inverse of the square of the distance from Kesh. It'd just be more cosmic background noise. Didn't they teach you anything where you came from?|Parrah, to Gloyd|<ref name="paragon" />}}
'''Ermon Parrah''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] relief [[Navigator/Legends|navigator]] for the [[Sith dreadnaught]] ''[[Omen]]'' during the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]]. In [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], after being knocked off-course during a [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] jump, the ''Omen'' crash-landed on the secluded [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]]. Parrah survived the disaster, and lived long enough to see the Sith worshiped as gods by the planet's natives, the [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. By [[4985 BBY]], Parrah had become the main science advisor to the Sith leader, [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Yaru Korsin]]. At some point prior to [[4975 BBY]], Ermon proposed to repair the ''Omen'' and return to the stars but this was denied by the current [[Grand Lord]]. In response, Ermon started a [[Parrah's rebellion|revolt]] and tried to steal the [[Starship/Legends|starship]]. However, he was defeated by the Grand Lord's forces.

Following the failed uprising, Parrah's conspirators and their families were enslaved and banished to the port town of [[Eorm]]. Meanwhile, Parrah and his descendants were forced to spin a cord that "would reach into space." Due to the physical impossibilities of such a task, Parrah's descendants were reduced to the status of paupers for millennia. They became known as the [[Spinner family]] due to their work as tailors and seamstresses. One of his descendants was [[Parlan Spinner]] who lived around [[2974 BBY]].

==Biography==
During the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]], Ermon Parrah, a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]], served the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] as the relief [[Navigator/Legends|navigator]] on the<ref name="paragon" /> [[Sith dreadnaught]]<ref name="crosscurrent">''[[Crosscurrent]]''</ref> ''[[Omen]]''. In [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], Parrah was aboard the ''Omen'' when it was knocked off course as it jumped to [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] during a [[Skirmish over Phaegon III|skirmish]] with [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] above the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Phaegon III]], where the ''Omen'' was stationed for a [[Mining/Legends|mining]] mission.<ref name="precipice">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Precipice]]''</ref> The damaged [[Starship/Legends|starship]] came out of hyperspace near an uncharted [[Planet/Legends|planet]], [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]]&mdash;the ''Omen'' was forced to crash-land in a large [[Takara Mountains|mountain range]]. Parrah survived the crash, and eventually the Sith came to be worshiped as [[Skyborn|gods]] by the planet's [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]] natives. By [[4985 BBY]], Ermon Parrah had become the main science advisor for the [[Lost Tribe of Sith|remaining Sith]], led by [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Yaru Korsin]]. That [[Standard year/Legends|year]], the [[Houk/Legends|Houk]] [[Gunner/Legends|gunner]] [[Gloyd]], still hoping to find a way off Kesh, proposed that the Sith use the ''Omen''{{'s}} surviving boring [[Laser/Legends|lasers]] to fire signals into [[Realspace/Legends|space]]. Parrah shot down the idea, knowing that the lasers would only dissipate into cosmic background noise before ever being noticed by anybody.<ref name="paragon" />

Ermon Parrah later participated during the [[Red Sith Purge]] on the side of Yaru Korsin. At some point prior to [[Seelah Korsin|Seelah]] and [[Jariad Korsin]]'s [[Duel near the Kesh Sith Temple|failed coup d'état]] against Korsin in [[4975 BBY]], he led a [[Parrah's rebellion|failed attempt]] to steal the crippled ''Omen'' and return to the stars.<ref>{{EmailCite|email=File:John Jackson Miller email Oct 19-20 001.jpg|creator=[[John Jackson Miller]]|date=2013-10-19}}</ref> However, the uprising was crushed by the Tribe's forces. As punishment, Parrah's supporters were [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] and became the first Human slaves on Kesh. Meanwhile, Parrah and all his descendants were forced to spin a cord that would reach the [[Star/Legends|stars]]. Since this task was physically impossible, Parrah and his descendants were condemned to millennia of slavery and became known as the [[Spinner family]]. For generations, the Spinner family worked as tailors and weavers in [[Eorm]], a port town that was home to exiled Sith and [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]] slaves. The Spinner family continued spinning the cord even during [[Time of the Rot|the Time of the Rot]], which saw a breakdown of law and order in [[Keshtah Minor]], the Tribe's domain.<ref name="Spiral 3">[[Lost Tribe of the Sith — Spiral 3|''Lost Tribe of the Sith — Spiral'' 3]]</ref>

One of Ermon Parrah's descendants was the Sith criminal [[Parlan Spinner]], who was the only person in the family line to rebel against this servitude. Following a failed attempt to assassinate the ruling [[Grand Lord]] [[Varner Hilts]] in [[2974 BBY]], Spinner awakened the ancient [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Remulus Dreypa]] and together the two Sith instigated an [[Dreypa's rebellion|uprising]] against the Tribe.<ref name="Spiral 3" /> However, he turned against Dreypa after the latter unleashed [[Leviathan (creature)|leviathans]], reptilian [[Sithspawn/Legends|Sithspawn]], that were capable of draining the souls of sentient beings. In the end, Spinner fulfilled his ancestor's ambition to "ascend" to the stars when he discovered an ancient [[Last Hope (Jedi starship)|Jedi starship]] beneath the Sith capital [[Tahv]]'s [[Circle Eternal]] plaza. Ultimately, Spinner became the savior of the Tribe when he defeated Dreypa at the cost of destroying the Jedi starship; setting back the Tribe's ambitions of reaching the stars until [[41 ABY|41.5 ABY]].<ref name="Spiral 5">[[Lost Tribe of the Sith — Spiral 5|''Lost Tribe of the Sith — Spiral'' 5]]</ref>

==Personality and traits==
Parrah was very knowledgeable in matters of cosmic science, enough so that he was made chief science advisor for the Sith on Kesh. However, when speaking to people who were not as well versed as he was, he could be somewhat condescending.<ref name="paragon" /> Throughout his life, Parrah harbored the ambition of returning to the [[Star/Legends|stars]]. This led him to lead a failed attempt to steal the ''Omen'' from the Sith Temple. However, he was defeated. As punishment for his brazenness, he and his descendants were condemned to generations of slavery.<ref name="Spiral 3" />

==Behind the scenes==
Ermon Parrah made his first appearance in the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] in [[John Jackson Miller]]'s [[2010]] [[eBook]] ''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Paragon]]''.<ref name="paragon" />

According to an [[:File:John Jackson_Miller_email_Oct_19-20_001.jpg|email exchange]] with Miller dating back to [[October 20]], [[2013]], Miller confirmed that the relief navigator Parrah and the Sith rebel Ermon Parrah were in fact the same person. He also clarified that [[Parrah's rebellion]] had occurred between the events of the two eBooks [[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Paragon|''Paragon'']] and [[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Savior|''Savior'']], since the comic ''Spiral 3'' depicted the [[Kesh Sith Temple]], which was sealed off after the events of ''Savior''. Miller has argued that the Lost Tribe of Sith did not kill Parrah because the Tribe was running out of Humans by that time. According to Miller, the script for ''Spiral 3'' had initially conceptualized Parrah fighting an older [[Yaru Korsin]]. However, Miller and his team opted not to name Parrah's opponent since he did not resemble the [[:File:Yaru Korsin.jpg|older version]] of the character in [[Pablo Hidalgo]]'s ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'', which was released on [[August 21]], [[2012]]. Thus, Miller has speculated that Parrah's opponent was actually one of Korsin's allies.<ref name="email">[[:File:John_Jackson_Miller_email_Oct_19-20_001.jpg|Email interview October 19-20, 2013]]</ref>
